summary: By the Sea of Galilee, Jesus fills Simon’s empty nets after a fruitless night and calls Simon, Andrew, James and John to follow Him and become fishers of men.
key_insight: Simon’s first response to the great catch was not delight but fear: “Depart from me, for I am a sinful man, O Lord!” Jesus answered with a call, not a departure. The man who asked Jesus to leave was the man Jesus took with Him.
story: One day Jesus was walking by the Sea of Galilee, {Mt} and a crowd was pressing around Him to hear the word of God. He saw two boats pulled up by the shore; the fishermen had left them and were washing their nets. {Lk}
Jesus got into one of the boats, which was Simon’s, and asked him to push out a little from the land. Then He sat down and taught the crowds from the boat. {Lk}

When He had finished speaking, He said to Simon, “Launch out into the deep and let down your nets for a catch.” Simon answered, “Master, we have toiled all night and caught nothing; nevertheless at Your word I will let down the net.” {Lk}
They caught so many fish that their net began to break. They signaled to their partners in the other boat to come and help, and they filled both boats until they began to sink. {Lk}

When Simon Peter saw it, he fell down at Jesus’ knees: “Depart from me, for I am a sinful man, O Lord!” He and all who were with him were astonished at the catch, and so were James and John, the sons of Zebedee, Simon’s partners. Jesus said to Simon, “Do not be afraid. From now on you will catch men.” {Lk}

To Simon and his brother Andrew, Jesus said, “Follow Me, and I will make you become fishers of men.” They immediately left their nets and followed Him. {Mk} A little farther on He saw James and John in the boat with Zebedee their father, mending their nets, {Mt} and He called them. They left their father Zebedee in the boat with the hired servants and went after Him. {Mk} The four forsook all and followed Him. {Lk}
differences: Matthew and Mark tell a brief call by the shore. Luke alone tells of the crowd, the teaching from Simon’s boat, the great catch and Simon’s confession.
In Matthew and Mark, Simon and Andrew are casting a net into the sea when Jesus sees them; in Luke the fishermen have left their boats and are washing their nets.
Matthew and Mark give the call as “Follow Me, and I will make you fishers of men” (Mark: “become fishers of men”); Luke gives Jesus’ word to Simon, “From now on you will catch men.”
Luke does not mention Andrew, and Matthew and Mark do not mention the catch. Only Mark mentions the hired servants left with Zebedee.

fit.question: Matthew and Mark tell of a short call by the shore. Luke tells of teaching from a boat, a miraculous catch and a call that follows it. Is this one call told two ways, or two stages of the same call?

points.label: One morning, told two ways
points.text: McGarvey and Edersheim both read the three accounts as one occasion. Matthew and Mark give the call in brief; Luke adds what happened around it. In every account the outcome is the same: the four leave their nets and follow Jesus.

points.label: Two stages
points.text: Others note that the scenes differ, casting nets in one and washing nets in the other, and that Luke places his account after Jesus had already been in Simon’s house (Luke 4:38). On this view, Jesus first called the brothers by the shore, they went back to fishing for a time, and the catch in Luke 5 settled the call for good.

points.label: Not their first meeting
points.text: On either reading, Andrew and Simon had met Jesus months earlier at the Jordan, where Jesus named Simon Cephas (John 1:35–42; see event 20). The call by the lake built on a friendship already begun.

fit.note: The Gospels do not say which reading is right. Neither one sets the accounts against each other, and each adds what the others leave out.
fit.short: Either one call, which Luke tells in full, or two stages: a first call by the shore, then the catch that settled it.

scene.label: The lake
scene.text: The Sea of Galilee, also called the Lake of Gennesaret, is a freshwater lake about 13 miles long and 8 miles wide, some 700 feet below sea level. Fishing was a main trade of the towns along its northern shore, including Capernaum and Bethsaida.

scene.label: Night fishing
scene.text: Fishermen on the lake usually worked at night (John 21:3) and cleaned and mended their nets in the morning. Simon knew the lake well. Letting down nets in deep water by daylight, after an empty night, went against everything his trade had taught him.

scene.label: Partners and hired servants
scene.text: Simon was in partnership with Zebedee’s sons, and Zebedee employed hired servants. This was a working family business of some size. Leaving the boats meant leaving a livelihood.

scene.label: “Follow Me”
scene.text: Jewish students usually sought out a teacher and asked to study with him. Jesus did the reverse: He chose His followers and called them. Following meant walking with Him, learning His ways and sharing His work.

witnesses.matthew: Places the call right after Jesus settles in Capernaum and begins to preach, so His first recorded act after that preaching is gathering followers. Matthew notes that James and John left “the boat and their father,” a costly break in a world built on family ties.
witnesses.mark: Tells it with speed: “immediately” they left and followed. Only Mark mentions the hired servants, so Zebedee was not left alone, a detail that reads like an eyewitness memory, likely Peter’s.
witnesses.luke: Gives the fullest scene: the crowd hungry for the word of God, the teaching from Simon’s boat, the catch and Simon’s confession of sin. Luke keeps the spotlight on Simon, who will lead the apostles in Acts, and shows his call beginning at Jesus’ knees.
witnesses.john: Does not record this event. John tells of an earlier meeting at the Jordan (John 1:35–42) and of a second great catch after the resurrection, when Jesus restored Peter (John 21:1–17).

seeing.reveals: Jesus is Lord of the lake Simon knew best. He commands the fish of the deep and the lives of men. In His presence Simon saw his own sin, and Jesus answered with grace: “Do not be afraid.”
seeing.living: Simon obeyed before he understood: “nevertheless at Your word.” Jesus meets people in their own work and their own failures, and calls them to something larger than both. Following Him may mean leaving the nets that once defined you.
seeing.ponder: Where, like Simon after a long empty night, do you need to say to Jesus, “nevertheless at Your word”?

preaching.big_idea: Jesus meets us in our empty nets and calls sinners to catch men.
preaching.watch_for: Simon’s name for Jesus changes from “Master” (5:5) to “Lord” (5:8). The catch moved him from respect for a teacher to awe before the holy One, much as Isaiah cried out when he saw the Lord (Isaiah 6:5).
